# UDreamThrobber

<!-- Generated by the DreamGUIReferenceDocs commandlet from reflection. Edit the header, not this page. -->

Inherits from [UDreamUIControl](DreamUIControl.md).

Declared in `Public/Controls/DreamThrobber.h`.

A throbber whose hierarchy is code, not an asset: N pieces that pulse, saying only "something is
happening".

ONE CONTROL FOR UMG'S TWO, which is the call this library has already made three times: the
progress bar has Bar and Radial rather than two classes, the slider has a Direction rather than
two Blueprint presets, the scroll box has an Orientation. The pieces, the period, the colours and
the fade are identical between a Throbber and a CircularThrobber; the only thing that differs is
where the pieces are put, so that is one enum and not one class. The palette still offers both
rows -- they differ by a single property write, exactly like the two sliders.

WHY IT TICKS, WHEN NOTHING ELSE IN THE LIBRARY DOES
---------------------------------------------------
Every other animated thing here is a TWEEN: it has a start, an end and a duration, and the tween
manager owns the clock. A throbber has none of those -- it runs until somebody takes it off screen
-- so a tween would have to be re-started forever, and a looping tween per piece would be N
objects the manager walks every frame to do arithmetic this control can do in one pass. So it opts
into NativeOnTick (off by default for every widget, see UDreamUserWidget::SetWantsTick) and writes
the opacities itself.

That also makes it correct where the tween manager does not exist: the manager is a world
subsystem and hands back null in a headless test and in the designer's preview, where a tween-based
throbber would simply stand still. This one animates wherever something calls its tick, and holds
its first frame where nothing does -- which is a throbber that LOOKS like a throbber in the
designer rather than an empty box.

NO PLAY / STOP, for UMG's reason: a throbber is not a timeline. Take it off screen to stop it.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Category | In the details panel | From Blueprint | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Style` | `FDreamThrobberStyle` | Throbber | yes | `GetStyle` / `SetStyle` | This instance's own look. The project sheet wins while StyleSource says so AND a sheet actually exists; with no sheet in the project this IS the look in effect. |
| `Shape` | `EDreamThrobberShape` | Throbber | yes | `GetShape` / `SetShape` | A row of pieces, or pieces around a circle. UMG's Throbber and CircularThrobber. |
| `bAnimate` | `bool` | Throbber | yes | `GetAnimate` / `SetAnimate` | Off holds the pieces at the phase they were on. The widget stops ticking with it. |
| `bAnimateHorizontally` | `bool` | Throbber | yes | `GetAnimateHorizontally` / `SetAnimateHorizontally` | Whether a piece also PULSES on that axis -- UMG's bAnimateHorizontally / bAnimateVertically, and Slate's rule for them: the piece is scaled on the ticked axis by the same wave that drives its opacity, so it swells as it brightens and shrinks as it fades. |
| `bAnimateVertically` | `bool` | Throbber | yes | `GetAnimateVertically` / `SetAnimateVertically` |  |
| `PieceRootNode` | `TObjectPtr<UDreamWidget>` | Throbber | - | read only | What the pieces hang under, and the control's one built-in node. |
| `PieceNodes` | `TArray<TObjectPtr<UDreamWidget> >` | Throbber | - | read only | The pieces, in order. Public because a decorator may want to skin one. |

| Function | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `bool GetAnimate()` | pure | Get Animate |
| `bool GetAnimateHorizontally()` | pure | Get Animate Horizontally |
| `bool GetAnimateOpacity()` | pure | Whether the pieces fade at all -- UMG's bAnimateOpacity, read off how faint they are allowed to get: a floor of 1 keeps every piece solid, which is the flag being off. |
| `bool GetAnimateVertically()` | pure | Get Animate Vertically |

| `float GetPhase()` | pure | How far through one cycle the animation is, 0 to 1. Authored in; readable out. |

| `FDreamThrobberStyle GetStyle()` | pure | Get Style |
| `void SetAnimate(bool bInAnimate)` | callable | Set Animate |
| `void SetAnimateHorizontally(bool bInAnimateHorizontally)` | callable | Turning it OFF re-places every piece at once, because a piece frozen mid-pulse would otherwise keep the width the last tick gave it -- a switch that leaves the thing it switched off in a random state is a switch that looks broken. |
| `void SetAnimateOpacity(bool bInAnimateOpacity)` | callable | Off pins the floor at 1. On restores the style's shipped floor, but only when the floor is currently 1 -- so switching off and on again is not a way to lose a hand-tuned value, and a throbber already fading keeps fading exactly as far as it did. |
| `void SetAnimateVertically(bool bInAnimateVertically)` | callable | Set Animate Vertically |
| `void SetNumberOfPieces(int32 InNumberOfPieces)` | callable | Rebuilds the piece pool, which is what a count IS here. |
| `void SetPeriod(float InPeriod)` | callable | Seconds for one full cycle. Drives the linear shape too, where UMG offers it only on the ring. |
| `void SetRadius(float InRadius)` | callable | How far out the pieces ride. Circular only, as in UMG; the linear shape ignores it. |
| `void SetShape(EDreamThrobberShape InShape)` | callable | Re-places every piece: the two shapes put them in different places, nothing else differs. |
| `void SetStyle(FDreamThrobberStyle InStyle)` | callable | This instance's whole look, replaced and pushed -- which for a throbber means the piece POOL is rebuilt if the count changed. See UDreamButton::SetStyle for the caveat about the sheet. |

## Compared with UMG

Every Blueprint-facing member of the UMG class, and where it went. *adopt*: same name, same meaning. *map*: here under another name or on another type. *reject*: deliberately absent, with the reason.

| UMG | Member | Status | Here | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `UCircularThrobber` | `NumberOfPieces` | map | `FDreamThrobberStyle::NumberOfPieces` | One control and one style for UMG's two throbbers; Shape = Circular is this class. |
| `UCircularThrobber` | `Period` | map | `FDreamThrobberStyle::Period` | Seconds for one full cycle, and it drives the linear shape too -- UMG only offers it on the circular one. |
| `UCircularThrobber` | `Radius` | map | `FDreamThrobberStyle::Radius` | How far out the pieces ride, measured from the middle. Circular only, as in UMG. |
| `UCircularThrobber` | `Image` | map | `FDreamThrobberStyle::PieceBrush` | See the Throbber table: a piece is a procedural rect, so the brush is its body texture. |
| `UCircularThrobber` | `SetNumberOfPieces` | adopt | `SetNumberOfPieces` | One control for UMG's two, so this is the same call the Throbber table lists. |
| `UCircularThrobber` | `SetPeriod` | adopt | `SetPeriod` | Drives the linear shape too, where UMG offers it only on the ring. |
| `UCircularThrobber` | `SetRadius` | adopt | `SetRadius` | Circular only, as in UMG; the linear shape ignores it. |
| `UCircularThrobber` | `bEnableRadius` | reject |  | The inline tick beside UMG's Radius, and Transient there: it exists so an unticked radius falls back to the Slate style's. A radius here is always the style's own number, so there is nothing for a tick to choose between. |
| `UThrobber` | `NumberOfPieces` | map | `FDreamThrobberStyle::NumberOfPieces` | In the style: how many dots a project's spinners have is a theme decision, and the control rebuilds its piece pool on every push. |
| `UThrobber` | `bAnimateHorizontally` | adopt | `bAnimateHorizontally` | Slate's rule, kept: the piece is SCALED on the ticked axis by the same wave that drives its opacity, so it swells as it brightens. One wave for both rather than a second clock. Off by default, which is what this throbber has always drawn. |
| `UThrobber` | `bAnimateVertically` | adopt | `bAnimateVertically` |  |
| `UThrobber` | `bAnimateOpacity` | map | `FDreamThrobberStyle::MinOpacity` | A float where UMG has a bool, and it says more: MinOpacity 1 is UMG's bAnimateOpacity off (every piece stays solid), and anything less is how faint a piece gets at the bottom of its cycle. GetAnimateOpacity / SetAnimateOpacity spell UMG's bool over it. |
| `UThrobber` | `Image` | map | `FDreamThrobberStyle::PieceBrush` | FDreamUIFaceBrush rather than FSlateBrush -- a piece is a procedural rect and the brush is its body texture. Empty is the plain rounded dot. |
| `UThrobber` | `SetNumberOfPieces` | adopt | `SetNumberOfPieces` | Rebuilds the piece pool, which is what a count IS here. Edits this instance's style; see UDreamBorder::SetPadding for the caveat about a project sheet. |
| `UThrobber` | `SetAnimateHorizontally` | adopt | `SetAnimateHorizontally` | Turning it off re-places every piece, so a piece frozen mid-pulse does not keep the width the last tick gave it. |
| `UThrobber` | `SetAnimateVertically` | adopt | `SetAnimateVertically` |  |
| `UThrobber` | `SetAnimateOpacity` | adopt | `SetAnimateOpacity` | Off pins the floor at 1; on restores the shipped floor only when the floor is currently 1, so switching off and on is not a way to lose a hand-tuned value. |
| `UThrobber` | `SetStyle` | adopt | `SetStyle` | UThrobber has no style struct; this is the family's spelling, and the one call that rebuilds the piece pool. |
